issues.title: e2e_node: make ImageGCPeriod (and other e2e_node wait budgets) configurable for tests
issues.body:
﻿## What happened
While removing duplicated `[Slow]` spec execution between `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-serial` and `ci-kubernetes-node-e2e-containerd-slow` (kubernetes/test-infra#37903), we looked into why the `[Slow]`-tagged ImageGC/GarbageCollect/MirrorPod specs in `test/e2e_node` cost ~30 minutes per host.

It's not image size or pull time — these use the standard few-MB e2e-test-images (pause, busybox, nginx-slim/agnhost). The time comes from wait/poll budgets hardcoded in the tests themselves, bound to production defaults:

- `image_gc_test.go`: two `[Slow]` specs poll for up to `checkGCUntil = 6 * time.Minute`, gated by kubelet's `ImageGCPeriod` (hardcoded to 5 minutes).
- `garbage_collector_test.go`: `setupDuration = 10 * time.Minute`, `garbageCollectDuration = 3 * time.Minute`.
- `mirror_pod_test.go`: several `2 * time.Minute` `Eventually` polls, plus a couple `5 * time.Minute` waits.

Polling more frequently doesn't help — these tests aren't slow because they check infrequently, they're waiting on a real kubelet-side event gated by a fixed period.

## What we'd like
Make `ImageGCPeriod` (and whatever governs the GC/mirror-pod wait windows above) configurable for e2e_node tests, so these specs aren't bound to the 5-minute production default and can run with a much shorter period in test.

## Context
- kubernetes/test-infra#37903 (merged) — removed duplicate execution of these specs as a stopgap
- kubernetes/kubernetes#142147 — the investigation that led here
- Requested by @kannon92 during the review of https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/37903

/kind feature

comments.author: harche
comments.body:
> I wasn't expecting product changes for this. Changing kubelet configuration is an api change.
> I think its fine to proceed but I'll want to loop in @haircommander, @harche and @SergeyKanzhelev to see if this is the path we want to take.

@ayanasarkar, thanks for putting the PR together so quickly. I agree with @kannon92 here. I don't think adding fields to KubeletConfiguration is the right path for this. Once they're in v1beta1 we support them indefinitely, and users will start tuning them on real nodes. A very short image GC period means repeated image listing and disk-stats work, and the 5 minute default exists to avoid that. That's a lot to take on to make a couple of `[Slow]` specs finish sooner.

I also wonder if we can get most of the same results without touching the API. I looked at where the time actually goes, and I'd love a second pair of eyes on this.

For image GC, the wait is real kubelet behavior. The loop runs every `ImageGCPeriod`, and the first pass after kubelet start deliberately skips age-based collection until `MaxAge` has passed:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9f929771aca0371445c821be11969220986a0639/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1761-L1781

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9f929771aca0371445c821be11969220986a0639/pkg/kubelet/images/image_gc_manager.go#L431-L433

The age logic itself is already covered by unit tests using a fake clock, which check both "not old enough" and "too old":

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9f929771aca0371445c821be11969220986a0639/pkg/kubelet/images/image_gc_manager_test.go#L780-L833

So the e2e only needs to prove the wiring works end to end, and it doesn't need two specs for that. "should not GC unused images prematurely" already ends with the same `Eventually` assertion as "should GC unused images", so it covers both cases. Would it make sense to drop the first spec, or fold it into the second? That saves one full ~6 minute wait without any product change.

For `garbage_collector_test.go`, I'm not sure `ContainerGCPeriod` is what's slowing us down. Setup waits for pods to reach their target restart counts, up to 4:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9f929771aca0371445c821be11969220986a0639/test/e2e_node/garbage_collector_test.go#L106

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9f929771aca0371445c821be11969220986a0639/test/e2e_node/garbage_collector_test.go#L179-L187

Reaching 4 restarts means going through CrashLoopBackOff (roughly 10s + 20s + 40s + 80s). Container GC already runs every minute, so dropping that to 10s probably saves under a minute. If we want this spec faster, could we lower the restart counts it needs? With `maxPerPodContainer = 1`, two or three restarts might be enough to exercise the same behavior. Happy to be corrected if I'm misreading the test.

The mirror pod waits aren't tied to a GC period at all, as the PR already notes, so they'd need separate treatment either way.

So my suggestion is to close #142570 and go with test-side changes: trim the duplicate image GC spec, look at the restart counts in the container GC test, and leave the rest under `[Slow]` in the dedicated job, where kubernetes/test-infra#37903 already removed the duplicate runs. Does that seem reasonable? @haircommander @SergeyKanzhelev, curious whether you see it differently.

issues.title: Stale repos - gopkg.in/inf.v0 (github.com/go-inf/inf)
issues.body:
Following the same pattern as #132312, for a different dependency.

`gopkg.in/inf.v0` is a **direct** dependency of `k8s.io/apimachinery`, where `inf.Dec` backs the arbitrary-precision path of `resource.Quantity`:

```go
type Quantity struct {
	// i is the quantity in int64 scaled form, if d.Dec == nil
	i int64Amount
	// d is the quantity in inf.Dec form if d.Dec != nil
	d infDecAmount
	...
}
```

It is also part of apimachinery's exported surface -- `func (q *Quantity) AsDec() *inf.Dec` and `func NewDecimalQuantity(b inf.Dec, format Format) *Quantity`, so it is compiled into essentially every Go program that talks to a Kubernetes API server, not only Kubernetes itself.

## What I am not claiming

There is no CVE (OSV reports zero for `gopkg.in/inf.v0`), no bug report, and no urgency. The package is 760 lines across `dec.go` and `rounder.go`, has **no external dependencies at all**, just `math/big`, `fmt`, `io`, `strings`, and uses neither `unsafe` nor `reflect`. Decimal arithmetic is a stable problem, and "no commits since 2018" is not by itself alarming for code of this shape. This is materially lower-risk than the json-iterator situation in #132312, and I do not think it should be treated with the same urgency.

I am also not proposing removal. `inf.Dec` is in a GA Go API on one of the most widely used types in the ecosystem, so removing it would need `k8s.io/apimachinery/v2`. That is not what this issue is asking for.

## What the actual concern is

It is bus factor, not code quality. As far as I can tell there is currently nobody able to publish a release under this import path:

- Last commit: **2018-03-27**. Last release: **v0.9.1, 2018-03-26**. Only two versions were ever tagged.
- Sole author is Péter Surányi (`@speter`, per the LICENSE copyright line); the only other commit in the repo's history is a one-line `gofmt` change from 2017. His last authored commit in any public repo is **2020-03-28**.
- The **`go-inf` organisation has zero public members**, no org email, and one repo. It was created in 2015 purely to back this vanity import path after Google Code shut down (see #26231). The original `speter.net` domain no longer resolves.
- [go-inf/inf#8](https://github.com/go-inf/inf/issues/8), "is it EOL ?", has been **open and unanswered since 2023-01-11**.
- [go-inf/inf#9](https://github.com/go-inf/inf/pull/9) was closed by its own author the day it was opened, unmerged, with no maintainer response.

So if a fix is ever genuinely needed under this path, a Go compatibility break, or an arithmetic bug found by the ongoing `Quantity` work, there is presently no mechanism to ship one, and downstream cannot route around it because the import path is in a public API.

I have tried the obvious things first: commented on go-inf/inf#8 on September, 05, 2026, and emailed the address in the repo's git history on September, 21, 2026. No response to either as of filing.

## The question

At what point, if any, is it worth acting on this proactively rather than waiting to need a fix we cannot ship? Roughly in increasing order of effort:

1. Someone with karma reaches Péter successfully and a maintainer gets added to `go-inf`, cheapest by far, and non-breaking, since the import path is unchanged.
2. Kubernetes adopts the package under an owned path, as was done for `google/gofuzz` → `sigs.k8s.io/randfill` and the `go-yaml` fork → `go.yaml.in/yaml`. The license is BSD-3, so this needs no one's permission, but note it is still a breaking Go API change, because `AsDec()` would return a different named type.
3. Deprecate `AsDec`/`NewDecimalQuantity` now and drop the dependency at a hypothetical apimachinery v2. Cleanest, slowest.

"The risk is acceptable, leave it alone" is a perfectly good answer too — I would just like it to be a decision on the record rather than something nobody has looked at. Happy to do the legwork on any of these if it is useful.

cc @thockin (you have both `dep-approvers` and `pkg/api/resource` hats, and may remember the 2016 `speter.net` migration) @dims (you filed #132312) @jpbetz (flagging so this does not surprise the `Quantity` burndown in #141166 — this issue is not a proposal to change that code)

issues.title: Add kubelet to KUBE_CGO_OVERRIDES in source-built race jobs once kubelet is a static binary
issues.body:
Follow-up from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135870, split out at @dims' request.

`-race` needs cgo, and [`kube::golang::build_binaries_for_platform()`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/79f041dd524968a26c28398be9b5dc30ada1f841/hack/lib/golang.sh#L841-L884) only appends `KUBE_RACE` to the non-static and `.test` groups, so a kubelet in `KUBE_STATIC_BINARIES` cannot carry race instrumentation at all. The DRA and kind race jobs already override the components they care about for exactly this reason:

```yaml
# Normally control plane components are linked statically, which does not work with -race (needs CGO).
# We need to override the default for components of interest.
- name: KUBE_CGO_OVERRIDES
  value: kube-apiserver kube-controller-manager kube-scheduler
```

kubelet is absent from that list only because it did not need to be there. Once #135870 merges, the build log line @pohly used to verify #133834 goes from `cmd/kubelet (non-static, race detection)` to `cmd/kubelet (static)` while `e2e.test` keeps its instrumentation, so those jobs stay green with an uninstrumented kubelet under test.

Adding `kubelet` to the override restores it, but only for the jobs that actually build it from source, which is worth being precise about:

- `dra-presubmit` and `dra-canary` set `kind_node_source=.`, and the kind CI and presubmit jobs go through `e2e-k8s.sh`, which runs `kind build node-image` against the checkout. kind forwards `os.Environ()` into the Kubernetes build and has `cmd/kubelet` among its targets, so the override reaches it.
- `dra-ci` points `kind_node_source` at a `dl.k8s.io` tarball and downloads `e2e.test`, so its `KUBE_RACE` and `KUBE_CGO_OVERRIDES` have nothing to act on. That is pre-existing and unrelated to #135870, but it does mean adding a name there would change nothing.
- Version-skew jobs copy a downloaded older kubelet onto the node after the build, so a build-time override does not affect what runs.

Happy to send the source-built part to kubernetes/test-infra so it can land alongside #135870 rather than after it.

/sig testing

kubernetes/test-infra#37840 merged, so the four source-built race jobs now carry `kubelet` in `KUBE_CGO_OVERRIDES`.

I traced the whole path before closing, since a config change on its own does not prove the override reaches the build. kind builds `cmd/kubelet` and hands `os.Environ()` to the Kubernetes build, `build/common.sh` forwards `KUBE_CGO_OVERRIDES` and `KUBE_RACE` into the build container, and on master the override puts kubelet back in the non-static group:

KUBE_RACE=-race make WHAT=cmd/kubelet
  cmd/kubelet (static)                        go install -installsuffix=static ...   no -race

KUBE_RACE=-race KUBE_CGO_OVERRIDES=kubelet make WHAT=cmd/kubelet
  cmd/kubelet (non-static, race detection)    go install ... -race
```

The other jobs that set `KUBE_RACE` do not build a kubelet: the ppc64le one sets it to the empty string with a TODO, the integration jobs do not build kubelet at all, and the release-branch jobs are on branches where kubelet is not in `KUBE_STATIC_BINARIES`.

Under `CGO_ENABLED=0` the file drops out of the build and `go test ./pkg/kubelet/cadvisor/` still reports ok, so nothing tells you it was skipped. 8cd98fbd60d relaxed the siblings back in 2019 and missed that one. issues.title: [Declarative Validation] Track beta→stable graduation of validation rules
issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

A tracking issue for the beta→stable graduation of declarative validation rules, per KEP-5073.

Every DV rule currently at beta carries `since: "1.37"`, and there are no older ones, so nothing was eligible until v1.37 shipped. It has, which opens the wave.

### Scope

Settled in [this comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/141532#issuecomment-5403123232):

- **One API type per PR**, not one group. The type is the kind: a nested struct such as `IPBlock` goes with `NetworkPolicy`, not in a PR of its own. Deleting handwritten validation has no per-rule rollback and costs the mismatch comparison its baseline, so diffs stay small enough to read line by line.
- **`+k8s:beta` to stable only.** Dropping the prefix. `+k8s:alpha` promotion is out of scope and handled separately.

- Before any rule gets here, it ran in Alpha/Beta alongside the handwritten check, where `VerifyValidationEquivalence` checks that handwritten and DV return the exact same errors (`mismatch_total == 0`).

issues.title: Burndown: Quantity int64 overflow and checked accessors
issues.body:
This tracks ongoing and planned work to fix `resource.Quantity`'s int64 accessor overflow behavior.

## Goal

Make `resource.Quantity` a value type that is safe to share between goroutines and correct for every input it accepts.

- Value type semantics. Changing a Quantity never changes another copy of it.
- Read-only methods never modify the Quantity, so concurrent reads are safe.
- Every method returns the same result whether the value is stored as int64 or `inf.Dec`.
- Arithmetic never wraps, and accessors report overflow or saturate.
- No input can make an operation use excessive CPU or take a long time to complete.
- Serialized output always reflects the current value and format.
- Data written by earlier releases still decodes, and every tightened check reuses one ratchet so existing objects stay updatable.
- Every fixed behavior and every open gap is pinned by a test on both backends.

## Known Gaps

| Expression | Returns | Gap |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NewScaledQuantity(MaxInt64, 1).Value()` | `-10` | multiply wraps around 64 bits |
| `MustParse("100E").Value()` | `0` | conversion fails internally and falls back to zero |
| `MustParse("9223372036854775808").Value()`| `MinInt64` | barely-too-large value becomes negative |
| `MustParse("-9.5Gi").Value()` | `8246196746` | bug in unsigned math flips the sign (#138510) |
| `NewQuantity(MinInt64).Neg()` | `MinInt64` | −MinInt64 doesn't fit in int64, so negation silently does nothing |
| `zero.Sub(MinInt64 quantity)` | `MinInt64` | similar to above, but using `.Sub()` instead of `.Neg()` |
| `MustParse("1000E").String()` | `"1"` | serialization drops the suffix for decimal values above 10^18 (#140459) |
| `ParseQuantity("1e4294967297")` | `10`, no error | exponent is truncated to 32 bits (2³²+1 → 1), should be parse error; #141203 rejected it, which created the decode row below; #142395 restores the 1.37 truncation for compatibility (09-24 decision); rejecting it is left to the 1.39 create-time bound |
| `NewQuantity(MinInt64).Neg(); q.AsInt64()` | `(MinInt64, true)` | `AsInt64` reports ok=true for a value that isn't the true result of the operation; same after `zero.Sub(MinInt64 quantity)` |
| `MustParse("1e100").Value()` vs `MustParse("1e100").ToDec().Value()` | `0` vs `MinInt64` | same input, different wrong values on the int64 vs Dec backends; fixes must land on both paths |
| decode of `"1e4294967296"` written by a <=1.37 apiserver | error, object undecodable | 1.37 truncated the exponent, kept value 1 and stored the spelling verbatim in JSON and proto; master rejects it in ParseQuantity (#141203); the etcd3 store fails the whole LIST on the first undecodable object. #142395 (approved 09-24) narrows the exponent the way 1.37 did, so these decode to the 1.37 value and keep their stored spelling; an exponent that narrows to MinInt32 still errors |
| `MustParse("1e2147483647").Add(MustParse("1"))` | hangs | the inf.Dec fallback aligns scales by writing 10^delta digits; same at Sub, AsScale/RoundUp, BinarySI String, AsFloat64Slow and DRA `quantityKeyAsDec`; reachable through pod-level resources validation and ResourceQuota admission; present in v1.37 and earlier |
| `MustParse("1e2147483647").Add(MustParse("1n"))` | `2e-9` | `int64Amount.Add/Sub` compute the scale delta in int32 and wrap instead of falling back; Cmp got this fix in #142013, Add/Sub did not |

comments.body:
Here is the `validateBasicResource` before/after I offered, measured rather than reasoned about. All of it is `apimachinery@v0.36.3`; the check itself is `quantity.Value() < 0` and nothing else (validation.go:8242).

"After" models the rule from the goal above — saturate at the int64 bound instead of wrapping — so a magnitude over `MaxInt64` becomes `MaxInt64`, and under `MinInt64` becomes `MinInt64`.

### What actually flips

Two cases out of everything I tried:

| input | `Value()` today | today | bounded |
| :--- | ---: | :--- | :--- |
| `NewScaledQuantity(MaxInt64, 1)` | `-10` | reject | **accept** |
| `MustParse("-1e30")` | `0` | accept | **reject** |

The first is the one the question is about. The second flips the other way and is a fix: a negative quantity that is accepted today starts being rejected.

### Why I do not think this is a protection worth preserving

The rejection is accidental, and measuring it shows how little it actually catches. Of the oversized positive inputs I tried, exactly two are rejected today — `NewScaledQuantity(MaxInt64, 1)` and `MustParse("9223372036854775808")`. These all pass validation right now:

```
MustParse("100E")                    Value() =                    0   accepted
MustParse("1000E")                   Value() =                    0   accepted
MustParse("5000E")                   Value() =                    0   accepted
MustParse("1e30")                    Value() =                    0   accepted
MustParse("18446744073709551616")    Value() =                    0   accepted
MustParse("8Ei")                     Value() =  9223372036854775807   accepted
MustParse("20Ei")                    Value() =  9223372036854775807   accepted
NewScaledQuantity(1, 21)             Value() =                    0   accepted
MustParse("1e4294967297")            Value() =                   10   accepted
```

So bounding does not take away a guard that works. It takes away one that fires on 2 of 11 oversized inputs, and only because the wrap happens to land on the negative side.

### The part that worries me more

The same check is already letting negative quantities through, and bounding does not fix it:

```
MustParse("-9.5Gi")            Sign() = -1   Value() =  8246196746   accepted
MustParse("-9.5000000001Gi")   Sign() = -1   Value() =  8246196746   accepted
MustParse("-1e30")             Sign() = -1   Value() =           0   accepted
MustParse("-100E")             Sign() = -1   Value() =           0   accepted
MustParse("-1000E")            Sign() = -1   Value() =           0   accepted
```

`Sign()` is right in every one of those; `Value()` is what lies. `-9.5Gi` is #138510, and `-1e30`/`-100E` are the "conversion fails, falls back to zero" gap. A negative resource quantity passing validation is worse than an oversized one passing, and it is happening today.

### Suggestion

Since the check only cares about the sign, `quantity.Sign() < 0` answers the question it is actually asking, without depending on any accessor's overflow behaviour. That closes all five of the negative cases above immediately, independently of the accessor work, and leaves bounding free to change `Value()` without touching validation semantics.

If oversized values should also be rejected, that reads like a separate, explicit limit rather than something to infer from a wrapped sign — and it would want its own decision about where the limit sits.

Happy to put the `Sign()` change up as its own PR with these cases as tests, or to leave it in the accessor work if you would rather it moved together.

> * **LimitRanger ([limitranger: compare resource quantities exactly to avoid int64 overflow #141348](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141348)).** Below a minimum the user raises the request and moves on. Above a maximum they can't. comments.body:
Went through #142224 with the stored-value cases in mind, since they are the ones that touch the API. Two things worth putting on the table before anyone resumes.

**Why those cases exist.** `18446744073709551616m` is 2^64 milli. In apimachinery v0.34.0 `MilliValue()` wraps and returns 0, so the pre-#141349 check (`MilliValue()%1000 != 0`) accepted it as an integer and it could be stored. On main `MilliValue()` saturates to MaxInt64, `AsMilliInt64` reports overflow, and `isIntegerResourceValue` rejects it. Every update of an object that holds such a value now fails with "must be an integer", which is what the `TestValidatePodTemplateUpdate` TODOs pin.

**How we have been fixing it.** Three hand-written ratchets in a week: #142170 for the PVC path in LimitRanger, #142171 for the pod path, and 1a39d08 (`isStoredQuantity`) for ResourceQuota, each with its own equality and its own plumbing, because `ValidatePodTemplateUpdate` does not pass the old object below `ValidatePodTemplateSpec`. The remaining TODOs (PodTemplate, RuntimeClass overhead, Node status) would add more copies. I think that is the API risk here, more than any single edge.

**What I would propose instead.** The precedent for "the stored object violates a check that has since tightened" is `PodValidationOptions`: `OldPodViolatesMatchLabelKeysValidation` and `AllowIndivisibleHugePagesValues` are computed once from the old spec in `GetValidationOptionsFromPodSpecAndMeta` and gate the check where it runs. The same shape works for quantities: a `StoredResourceQuantities` set built from the old spec, checked in `validateResourceRequirements` before `ValidateResourceQuantityValue`. Prototyped, +61/-2, no new plumbing. Through the real `podtemplate` strategy path: an unchanged stored 2^64m passes, changing it to 1.5 is still rejected, changing it to 2 passes, and create with 2^64m is still rejected. `pkg/apis/core/validation`, `pkg/registry/core/{pod,podtemplate}` and `pkg/api/pod` are green.

One consequence for #142224: the TODO cases call `ValidatePodTemplateUpdate` with an empty `PodValidationOptions{}`, so an options-based ratchet is invisible to them by construction; they would need to build options the way the `OldPodViolates*` tests do. Longer term the `EachMapVal` ratchet in `apimachinery/pkg/api/validate` is the same primitive, and this is where the declarative migration would land it.

Happy to open this as a PR against the PodTemplate TODOs once #142224 is in, or to hold it if you would rather handle these case by case.

issues.title: Add back `admissioninitializer.WantsAuthorizer` for v1.37
issues.body:
As part of implementing [Conditional Authorization](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5681), in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138801 we did a literal rename from 

```go
if wants, ok := plugin.(WantsAuthorizer); ok {
	wants.SetAuthorizer(i.authorizer)
}
```

to

```go
if wants, ok := plugin.(WantsUnconditionalAuthorizer); ok {
	wants.SetUnconditionalAuthorizer(i.authorizer)
}
```

using a fully mechanical rename, with `authorizer.UnconditionalAuthorizer` corresponding to the authorizer interface that existed in v1.36, and `authorizer.Authorizer` growing new capabilities in v1.37.

The intention was to add `admissioninitializer.WantsAuthorizer` in a subsequent PR as a clean diff to show new usage of new features. 

If commit https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/833f712b4259a5a18a4bd4aee078f422dd3ec776, admission plugins that provide `SetAuthorizer(authorizer.Authorizer)` in v1.36 would either:

a) get a compile error in v1.37 if they locked their implementation like `var _ admissioninitializer.WantsAuthorizer = fooPlugin{}`
b) fail silently at runtime during `ValidateInitialization() error` as `SetAuthorizer` wouldn't be called

...until the admission plugin performed the same rename.

This code was initially part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137633 (and its prefactor https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140715), but given this larger feature PR will not be part of v1.37, I propose to break out the commit to a dedicated PR, which targets v1.37 as a bug fix, to not break existing clients that depended on `admissioninitializer.WantsAuthorizer`.

/kind cleanup
/assign

issues.title: E2E Test Flakiness: API Server Timeouts, Silent Failures, and Resource Cleanup Issues
issues.body:
The e2e test framework has several patterns that cause flakiness, silent resource leaks, and hard-to-debug failures, especially in disruptive tests that restart API servers or control plane components. PR 137832 addresses these across 13 files (185 additions, 41 deletions), touching SIG api-machinery, apps, cloud-provider, network, node, storage, and testing.

Error suppression hides resource leaks. Across the test suite, cleanup code discards errors from Delete calls. In test/e2e/apimachinery/aggregator.go, the cleanupSampleAPIServer function has 10 such calls (APIService, Deployment, Secret, Service, ServiceAccount, RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding, ClusterRole) all silently swallowed. Same pattern in test/e2e/apimachinery/apply.go (4 deployments/pods), test/e2e/apps/rc.go (DeleteCollection), and test/e2e/apps/statefulset.go (ConfigMaps in defer blocks). When these fail, resources leak into subsequent tests with zero trace of what went wrong.

No retry on transient API server errors. GetControlPlaneNodes in test/e2e/framework/util.go calls Nodes().List() and immediately fails on any error. During disruptive tests (daemon restarts, etcd failure injection), the API server is expected to be briefly unreachable. The same issue exists in allNodesReady at test/e2e/framework/node/helper.go and RestartNodes at test/e2e/common/util.go. A transient connection refused or 503 kills the entire test instead of retrying. The fix introduces IsRetryableAPIError which checks for connection refused/reset, server timeout, 429, 503, 500, and unexpected server errors, plus a new WaitForControlPlaneNodes that wraps the listing in a polling loop with retry-on-transient logic.

Healthz returns 200 before daemon is ready. RestartDaemonConfig.waitUp in test/e2e/apps/daemon_restart.go considers the daemon ready when /healthz returns HTTP 200. After a kubelet restart, the health endpoint can report ok while kubelet is still recovering. Logs show errors, pods are not yet scheduled. The fix adds verifyDaemonReadiness which SSHes into the node and checks the last 20 lines of /var/log/kubelet.log for error patterns before declaring readiness.

Goroutines not gracefully stopped. In test/e2e/apps/daemon_restart.go, a cache.NewInformer controller is started with go controller.Run(backgroundCtx.Done()). The cleanup calls cancel() but does not wait for the controller goroutine to finish. The fix replaces this with a dedicated stopCh channel and DeferCleanup that closes the channel then sleeps 100ms to allow graceful shutdown.

PVC deletion races with pod references. DeleteAllStatefulSets in test/e2e/framework/statefulset/rest.go has a TODO comment about not checking whether pods still reference PVCs before deleting them. The current code deletes PVCs immediately, which can fail or leave orphaned PVs when pods are still running. The fix lists pods, checks volume references, and only deletes PVCs that are not in use, with foreground propagation.

Duplicated control plane filtering. GetControlPlaneNodes and WaitForControlPlaneNodes both contain the same node filtering logic (check for control-plane label and NoSchedule taint). The second commit extracts this into a shared filterControlPlaneNodes helper.

All changes are in e2e test code, no user-facing impact.

Related issues:
- 109600: prevent the Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred()) and ExpectNoError(err) anti-pattern in e2e tests (same category of error handling problems)
- 86253: sample-apiserver returns error instead of falling back to second Accept type (directly affects the aggregator.go test modified in this PR)
- 135285: GOAWAY are not handled gracefully in apiserver when aggregating (related network error handling)
- 105536: Orphaned pod found, but error not a directory occurred when trying to remove the volumes dir (related resource cleanup issue)

issues.title: Evaluate enforcement of `+listType=map` and `+listMapKey=uid` for OwnerReference in ObjectMeta
issues.body:
### What happened?
During the review of PR #140381 (Configure DV on objectMeta OwnerReference), it was observed that `OwnerReference` in `ObjectMeta` has the following tags in `staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/types.go`:
```go
// +patchStrategy=merge
// +listType=map
// +listMapKey=uid
```
However, there are currently no corresponding handwritten validations that fully enforce these constraints. 

### Why was this not addressed in PR #140381?
As discussed in [this comment thread](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140381#discussion_r3572186534), adding Declarative Validation (DV) for these markers right now could potentially break existing workflows. The scope of PR #140381 was strictly limited to mirroring the existing handwritten validations to ensure exact structural error reporting and deduplication parity.

### Action Items
- [ ] Investigate the impact of fully enforcing `+listMapKey=uid` and `+listType=map` on `OwnerReference`.
- [ ] Determine a safe rollout strategy if we decide to enforce these validations.
- [ ] Alternatively, if they should remain unenforced, add appropriate comments/documentation explaining this limitation.

/sig api-machinery
/kind cleanup
